text:
kevin: Heads-up — noticed cache reuse drop for /v1/generate on model-ambassador when stickiness is disabled. hit-rate down ~22% vs baseline. anyone seen this pattern before?

sana: yep saw a blip in dashboards yesterday, thought it was churn from new routing. do you have examples?

kevin: past 3h sample: requests with identical prompt-prefixes but different session ids are not reusing prefix entries. logs show many tiny entries (len<64B) getting churned.

jules: can you paste a small stack of the cache key format you're using?

kevin: sure — current key = join([route, model, session_id, hash(prefix)])

anika: hmm session_id in the key will prevent cross-session reuse by design. is that intentional?

kevin: it was added to avoid cross-customer leakage after the multi-tenant change. but for public routes we may want a separate opt-in mode.

perf-bot: perf/kv-cache: baseline reuse=0.62, today=0.48, median p95 latency +4ms on tail, memory growth steady but fragmentation metric increase +12%.

jules: that fragmentation % is the smoking gun. small keys + short-lived per-session entries cause allocator fragmentation. we should prefer canonicalized prefix keys not including session_id for shared reuse.

anika: privacy note — we can't store raw prefixes across sessions for tenant isolation. two ideas: 1) prefix fingerprinting (H(prefix) with per-tenant salt) and store only the fingerprint, 2) two-tier cache: shared fingerprint cache + per-session pointer layer.

kevin: agreed on privacy constraint. proposal: compute short fingerprint = murmur64(prefix_trimmed) then key = route|model|fingerprint. keep a separate per-session bloom filter to avoid accidental leakage on cold starts.

sana: can you show the config?

kevin: pasted config snippet we prototyped:
```
kv_cache:
  key_components: [route, model, fingerprint]
  fingerprint:
    algo: murmur64
    normalize: true
  session_layer:
    enabled: true
    bloom_size: 4096
```

jules: curious about collisions — murmur64 collisions are low for our prefix space, but we should add a short TTL for shared entries and conservative eviction to limit risk. also track prefix->example mapping in an audit log with access controls.

anika: TTL of 30m for shared prefix cache + per-session TTL of 5m for pointers seems reasonable. that reduces lifecycle and memory pressure.

perf-bot: sim-run #42 with prototype: reuse up +18%, token-cost down ~6%, end-to-end p95 latency -3ms. memory resident pages down ~4% and fragmentation index reduced by ~9%.

sana: nice. what about batching impact? if many sessions share same fingerprint, batching should improve throughput — did sim cover that?

kevin: yes sim included batch coalescing for identical prefix fingerprints; observed 7% better GPU utilization during peak.

jules: open question: how do we handle mutable prefixes (prompts that include timestamps or ephemeral IDs)? normalization layer needs heuristics — strip UUIDs, timestamps, emails. maybe a rule-based sanitizer + ML fingerprint fallback.

anika: can we ship a conservative sanitizer set first (timestamps, iso-dates, email regex, long hex ids)? iterate with evals to catch false-positives.

kevin: action items: 1) prod canary of fingerprint-only shared cache on low-traffic route (assign: kevin) 2) implement sanitizer rules and add unit tests (assign: jules) 3) telemetry: add tag to cache hit logs indicating "shared-fingerprint" vs "session-local" (assign: sana) 4) security review for fingerprint salt lifecycle (assign: anika).

jules: I'll start sanitizer PR and include collision+privacy tests.

anika: I'll prep security checklist and verify salt rotation plan + KMS usage.

kevin: I'll wire the canary and the sim harness. let's reconvene after 24h canary. thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: created perf job 1795012345-42; will post results to #eng-runtime/perf-runs when complete.
